title: Car Charging Stations
desc: Plan, site and run a small public or shared EV charging point: demand, power, safety, pricing, uptime and users.
outcomes: Explain charger types, connectors and grid limits.
Choose a site and size the supply.
Judge safety, cost, uptime and fairness.
Write a site plan and operations sheet.
task: Plan one charging point or small hub with site survey, power sizing, safety plan, tariff, maintenance plan and 12-month cash view.
condition: A computer, a map, a spreadsheet, two peers and a licensed electrician mentor. No live installation work is done by learners.
standard: Power and demand maths is correct; protective devices and earthing are listed and approved by a licensed person; accessibility is planned; uptime target and tariff shown; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Site hosts, shop and hotel owners, utilities assistants, installers.
evidence: site survey, sizing sheet, safety plan, tariff, maintenance plan, cash view
modules: AC points (3 to 22 kW) suit long stays; DC fast chargers suit quick stops.
Connectors and standards depend on region.
A mall installs 7 kW points because shoppers stay two hours.
Table includes time to add 30 kWh.
Visible, safe, lit, accessible, near amenities.
Distance to the electricity supply; transformer capacity.
Permissions from the owner and the utility.
A site 20 m from the panel cuts cable cost.
Total kW = chargers x kW x diversity factor.
Check supply capacity; add load management if limited.
Four 7 kW points on a 20 kW supply use load sharing.
Utilisation = hours in use / hours open.
Revenue = kWh sold x price minus electricity cost.
At 15% utilisation a 7 kW point sells about 9 kWh a day.
RCD protection, earthing, surge, emergency stop, fire plan.
A charger fails a test and is locked out until fixed.
Per kWh, per minute, session fee, idle fee.
An idle fee after 30 minutes frees the bay.
Remote monitoring; a fault response time.
A 24-hour fix target is met 95% of the time.
Everyone should be able to charge.
Share the plan with the community.
Wider bays and a call button suit wheelchair users.
quiz: Charge for occupying a bay after charging.
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: electric car basics, portable charging, solar basics.
local: Utility and safety rules differ by place.
ladder: L1: learner can name charger types.
L3: learner can survey a site.
L4: learner can run a site.
L6: learner can lead a small team.
L7: learner can audit a site plan.
